Bootstrap the edges of a heterogeneous transition network

Source: R/bootstrap_htna.R
bootstrap_htna.Rd

bootstrap_htna() bootstraps the edges of a heterogeneous transition network, or of every cohort of a grouped network, to show which transitions would reappear in another sample of sessions. The non-parametric bootstrap resamples the sessions with replacement, re-estimates the network on each resample, and summarizes the distribution of every edge weight: its mean, standard deviation, percentile confidence interval, and a p-value. An edge weight estimated from a sample of sessions is uncertain, and a plot of the network alone does not show that uncertainty.

Under the default inference = "stability", the p-value is the share of resamples (plus one, over the number of resamples plus one) whose weight falls outside a consistency range around the observed weight (by default 75 to 125 percent of it); an edge with a p-value below ci_level is reproduced by the resamples and is marked significant. The bootstrap works at the level of individual codes and runs Nestimate's bootstrap_network() with the actor partition kept, so plot_htna_bootstrap() draws the result with the actor layout and colours. bootstrap() is the generic, with a method for htna networks. It returns an htna_bootstrap object, or one per cohort for a grouped network.

For a closed-form estimate of the same quantities use certainty_htna(); to remove unstable edges use prune_htna() with method = "bootstrap"; for the stability of centralities use centrality_stability_htna().

Usage

bootstrap_htna(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna'
bootstrap(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna(), or an htna_group, in which case every cohort is bootstrapped.

...

Settings: iter (resamples, default 1000), ci_level (0.05), inference ("stability" or "threshold"), consistency_range (c(0.75, 1.25)), edge_threshold, seed, boundary, ci_method and actor (resample whole actors instead of sessions).

Value

For a network, an object of class c("htna_bootstrap", "net_bootstrap") with print(), summary() and plot() methods. summary() returns a data frame with one row per edge and columns from, to, weight, mean, sd, p_value, sig, ci_lower, ci_upper, cr_lower and cr_upper. For an htna_group, a named list of such objects with class c("htna_bootstrap_group", "list").

Conditions

An error of class htna_bad_input is raised when x is neither an htna network nor a list of them.

See also

plot_htna_bootstrap(), certainty_htna(), prune_htna(), reliability_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net  <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
boot <- bootstrap_htna(net, iter = 50, seed = 1)
boot
#>   Edge                   Mean     95% CI          p
#>   -----------------------------------------------
#>   Delegate → Plan        0.614  [0.563, 0.672]  *
